Thought: I need to determine what type of reaction occurs when acetylene reacts with strong bases. Let me analyze each option.

Acetylene (C₂H₂) is a terminal alkyne with the structure HC≡CH. It has acidic hydrogen atoms due to the triple bond, which makes the C-H bonds more acidic than typical C-H bonds.

When acetylene reacts with a strong base (like NaH, NaNH₂, or n-BuLi), the base removes a proton from acetylene, forming an acetylide ion (HC≡C⁻). This acetylide ion can then form a salt with the cation of the base, such as sodium acetylide (HC≡C⁻Na⁺).

This reaction is classified as an acid-base reaction resulting in acetylide salt formation.

Looking at the options:
A. Acetylide salt formation - This matches the reaction described.
B. Amide formation - This would involve nitrogen compounds, not relevant here.
C. Ester formation - This would involve carboxylic acids and alcohols, not relevant here.
D. Ether formation - This would involve alcohol reactions, not relevant here.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
